extraction.Name: Emma Running Hawk—nee Marrow Bone
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want her patent in fee to her 320 acre allotment, when it was issued, September 29, 1919, but the Indian Office told her that, if she did not take it, and pay the taxes, it would be taxed just the same, and later sold for taxes, so she took the patent
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: sold her allotment to Walcott & Walcott, of Valentine, Nebraska, for $1000.00 cash
extraction.Buyer: Walcott & Walcott, of Valentine, Nebraska, for $1000.00 cash
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: could not keep up the taxes on it, hence was forced to sell
extraction.NOTES: Mentally incompetent; has rheumatism, which makes it hard for her to get around, otherwise her health is good; mother of two minor children, one with good health, the other with poor eye sight and cannot go to school; husband has good health, works at common labor, and receives $80.00 per year lease money on his allotment, supports her and the children; these two sources of income is all they have; did not sell her allotment for any debts incurred prior to the receipt of the patent in fee; has never received any help from the United States Government, the State Government nor the County; allotment was 320 acres; document sworn March 21, 1929
